subject: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & data handling

Subject: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & data handling

Hi Anna — great to meet you and the team on today's call. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed: 

1) PII & retention
- You confirmed FinTrust considers transaction-level customer names and account numbers as PII; retention window target is 13 months for logs and 7 years for transactional records.
- Action: I'll confirm our default retention settings and options for customer-configurable retention.

2) Logging & auditability
- You asked for audit logs for both tenant activity and admin/support access, exportable in CSV/JSON.
- Action: we can provide syslog exports and a downloadable audit bundle; Nikhil will add a note on retention and format.

3) Data residency
- Primary requirement: all production inference must run in us-east-1; FinTrust may require a private VPC option for critical workloads.
- Action: we'll outline Dedicated vs Private deployment options for data residency and network controls.

4) Access controls (RBAC, least privilege, support access, break-glass procedures)
- You requested role-based policies with least-privilege defaults and a documented break-glass flow (two-person approval, audit trail).
- Action: Nikhil — can you draft the RBAC roles and break-glass procedure we typically propose?

Next steps:
- I will attach a short summary PDF with our typical controls (attached).
- Nikhil to share a draft RBAC matrix and break-glass procedure by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposed follow-up: security sync w/ your security team early next week (CC: security@fintrust.com).

If I've missed anything from the call, please flag. Thanks again — looking forward to lining up the security review.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: 13 months for system logs is a hard requirement; for request/response content we need to be able to configure retention to 30 days or longer depending on the dataset.
- KMS/HSM: we require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for encryption at rest for production PII.
- Support access: break-glass must generate an immutable audit entry with the justification, approver, and timestamps; prefer that approval be from a designated security contact or via our ticketing system.
- RBAC: we want pre-defined roles (read-only, app-admin, infra-admin, support-limited) and ability to add custom roles scoped to routes/models.

Attached is our security questionnaire (partial) — please fill in sections on KMS, logging exports, and support access. We are targeting a procurement decision by end of August, so timeline is tight.

Anna
Anna Lopez

Marissa — draft below and link to a short doc with the RBAC matrix: https://drive.google.com/fintrust-poc-plan (internal draft, will tighten).

RBAC (high level):
- Roles: read-only, app-admin, infra-admin, support-limited, auditor.
- Least privilege defaults: support-limited only receives a scoped token limited to customer troubleshooting routes (no access to raw request payloads), and all elevated actions require justification.

Break-glass:
- Mechanism: temporary privileged token issuance via console or API that requires two-step approval (on-call + security approver) OR an auto-approved flow if the request comes with a ticket from FinTrust's authenticated ticketing integration.
- Audit: every break-glass event logs user, approver(s), justification, TTL, and automatic export to audit bundle (CSV/JSON) retained for 13 months.

KMS/BYOK:
- We support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (AWS KMS with customer key policy); HSM-backed keys supported via partner integrations — we'll confirm SLA and attestation docs.

I'll clean this up and add explicit API/config examples by EOD.

—Nikhil

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: FinTrust - follow-up on access controls & data handling

Anna — thanks for the fast turnaround and the questionnaire. Summary answers below (high-level) and attached is our one-pager + the draft RBAC matrix Nikhil prepared.

- Retention: audit logs - configurable, default retention 13 months; request/response content - configurable per-customer with policy enforcement (can be set to 30 days minimum or longer).
- KMS/BYOK: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) and can integrate with HSMs via partner stack; we will provide KMS attestation and integration notes for your security team.
- Support access & break-glass: proposed flow is two-person approval (support engineer + security approver) OR pre-authorized ticket-based approval from your ticketing system. Every event produces an immutable audit bundle (user, approvers, justification, timestamps, TTL) exported on-demand and retained for 13 months.
- RBAC: we propose these base roles: read-only, app-admin, infra-admin, support-limited, auditor. Roles can be scoped to routes/models and custom roles can be created via the console/API.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the completed sections of your security questionnaire and the RBAC matrix to the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/fintrust-poc-plan).
2) Connor will produce a short TCO note for Dedicated vs Private with BYOK considerations by Friday.
3) Let's schedule a 30-min security sync with your SecOps next week to walk through the details and any docs you need for procurement. Please propose 2 windows that work for your team.

Happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Best,
